transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CompassMedix CTO), Priya Nair (Head of ML), Samir Gupta (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
CompassMedix is planning a renewal and wants to expand footprint to EU (and potentially APAC). They are considering a mix of reserved capacity + burst. Primary concerns: latency SLOs for EU users, data residency, SOC2 evidence, and predictable unit cost. Action items include pricing send, technical benchmark, and contract amendment draft.

Topics: capacity uplift, regional activation (eu-west + eu-central), contract term and amendment, security controls (KMS, SOC2), benchmarking prompts, fallbacks between hosted/dedicated.

Transcript:
[00:00:02] Maya: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining. i'm maya from redwood, i'll kick us off. hey jordan, priya, samir, can you hear me okay?
[00:00:10] Jordan: yep loud and clear, thanks maya.
[00:00:12] Priya: yes, all good here.
[00:00:14] Maya: great. quick agenda — align on renewal term, talk about the eu expansion requests, run through the latency and throughput targets you gave us, and then ethan will outline the benchmark plan. anything else to add?
[00:00:25] Samir: maybe quick note on security — we need the kms/keys workflow spelled out. also retention and audit logs.
[00:00:30] Maya: noted, we'll cover that.
[00:00:33] Jordan: great. high level — we are 9 months into the deployment. overall usage has grown faster than we expected. we want to lock in capacity for next year and add EU regions because a chunk of our traffic is Europe-based. also exploring APAC later but that's lower priority.
[00:00:50] Maya: perfect. can you restate the numbers you're thinking about for reserved vs burst? last sheet you sent had a rough RPS and token estimate.
[00:00:58] Priya: yeah, so baseline is about 60 requests per second, average payload ~350 tokens, peak bursts closer to 220 rps for events. we'd like reserved to cover 75% of baseline and burst covers spikes.
[00:01:10] Ethan: quick clarifying q — those peak bursts are sustained for how long typically? minutes? tens of minutes?
[00:01:16] Priya: usually 10-25 minutes, rare longer.
[00:01:20] Ethan: okay that matters a lot for provisioning and autoscaling. with our dedicated pools we can guarantee steady throughput and then burst to hosted capacity if needed, or we can set a cushion in the commit.
[00:01:31] Jordan: what's the typical failover — if a region is saturated do requests route to another region? we need to keep latency low for EU users.
[00:01:38] Ethan: by policy we can route by latency and prefer regional instances; fallback would go to a compatible model variant in another region which increases p50/p90 by usually 40-120ms depending on distance. we also support cross-region KV cache warmups to reduce cold-cache penalties but that depends on stateful policies.
[00:01:54] Priya: hmm 120ms might be noticeable for some usecases, what's our SLA target we can guarantee with a dedicated pool?
[00:02:01] Maya: our SLA for dedicated is 99.95% uptime and typical p95 latency targets we publish per model and profile; ethan, can you speak to numbers for the medium-length prompts?
[00:02:10] Ethan: for the models you're using (we validated the 7B family and the 13B variant) p95 token latencies on EU dedpods are generally in the 230-420ms range depending on sequence lengths and KV cache hit rate. If you pin to a quantized variant we can shave cost but need to validate quality.
[00:02:29] Jordan: okay. our UX team says keeping p95 under 400ms for user-facing flows is priority. any recommendations?
[00:02:35] Ethan: keep KV cache warm for session flows, use a dedicated pool sized for baseline, and set the autoscale policy to pre-warm a small buffer. Also we can recommend a slightly smaller model variant for latency-sensitive paths and keep the larger model for backend or async tasks.
[00:02:50] Priya: we were worried about quantization impacting accuracy on medical classification prompts — our evals are sensitive. can we run a small eval?
[00:02:58] Maya: absolutely, that's one of the next steps — SE-run evals against your prompt set. we'll include quality checks and regression thresholds.
[00:03:05] Jordan: security wise, Samir mentioned kms. can you outline how Redwood integrates with customer-managed keys?
[00:03:12] Ethan: sure — we support KMS/HSM integration for private deployment and for Redwood Private we can configure CMKs. For hosted there's envelope encryption with customer-provided keys via the cloud provider KMS if you choose BYOK; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. i'll note that some of these flows differ for dedicated vs hosted.
[00:03:30] Samir: do you have SOC2 artifacts we can share with our auditors?
[00:03:33] Maya: yes we have SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation artifacts — i'll put them in the shared folder. we'll also include the network diagram for the VPC peering flow.
[00:03:42] Jordan: ideal. about data residency — for EU we need logs retained in-region for 90 days and for certain datasets 7 years, is that supported?
[00:03:50] Ethan: we can keep logs in-region if you use dedicated or private; hosted has options for geo-retention but there are nuances, we'll surface them in the security doc we share.
[00:03:59] Priya: pricing is the other big point — can you run through reserved commit impact vs pure on-demand? our finance team wants predictability.
[00:04:06] Maya: sure. reserved capacity gives you a lower per-token and per-request unit, and predictable egress. burst pricing applies when usage exceeds the commit. we can show blended scenarios. we'll send a matrix showing baseline commit levels (50%, 75%, 100%) with projected monthly cost and burst overage sensitivity.
[00:04:24] Jordan: do you offer seat discounts or multi-year pricing?
[00:04:27] Maya: yes, 12-month renewal gets a modest discount vs month-to-month. multi-year we'll need legal to weigh in, but typically there's a tiered discount structure. i'll include sample amendments.
[00:04:37] Samir: latency test — can you run a benchmark from our eu-west region with our production-ish payloads?
[00:04:43] Ethan: yes we'll provision a harness. request: can you drop the prompt set (anonymized) in the shared drive and provide the expected distribution (seq lengths, session vs stateless)? also ssh jump or test endpoints?
[00:04:56] Priya: we'll anonymize and upload by end of day. sequence distribution is heavy around 300 tokens and a long tail to 1.2k for some documents.
[00:05:05] Ethan: good to know. for the long-tail we should test memory/kv caching behavior. we'll run both cold and hot-cache runs.
[00:05:11] Jordan: what's the lead time to spin up eu dedicated nodes if we sign the amendment?
[00:05:15] Maya: typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for capacity to be provisioned and tested in-region; if you need a faster path we can do a hybrid — start with hosted region activation (same models) and then flip to dedicated when available.
[00:05:27] Jordan: ok 2-4 weeks is workable but we need ramp plans.
[00:05:30] Maya: we'll include a ramp plan in the contract amendment — initial baseline, test window, cutover, rollback plan.
[00:05:36] Priya: about fallbacks — if dedicated saturates, can we route some requests to a cheaper, smaller model variant to keep latency low?
[00:05:43] Ethan: yes policy-based routing supports model variants and quality-preserving fallbacks. you can specify thresholds and percentage rollbacks. we'll show config examples in the ops playbook.
[00:05:52] Samir: curious on tokenization differences — we run some pretokenization and other platforms' tokenizers differ slightly. any gotchas?
[00:05:58] Ethan: tokenizer differences can change token counts and therefore cost; we can run tokenization parity checks and provide a mapping. usually <3% variance but depends on your preprocessing.
[00:06:09] Jordan: sounds good. let's talk timeline — we want to finalize commit by end of month to lock rates. can you make that feasible?
[00:06:16] Maya: yes, if you confirm the RPS and regions this week and we get sign-off on contract terms by 8/25, we can have eu provisioning started 8/26 and initial test cluster in early september.
[00:06:28] Priya: finance will need a clear projection. can you include a 12-month and 24-month projection with conservative and aggressive growth scenarios?
[00:06:36] Maya: absolutely. we'll provide three scenarios and show blended pricing for reserved+burst.
[00:06:41] Ethan: i want to highlight a technical caveat — if your burst pattern has frequent 1-2 minute spikes, autoscaler behavior and cold-start impact matters; we'll include recommended autoscale/queue sizes to keep p95 under your 400ms constraint.
[00:06:54] Samir: noted. on the security doc, please include the KMS rotation cadence and how keys are revoked if needed.
[00:06:59] Maya: will do.
[00:07:02] Jordan: anything on the contract side around liability for model regressions? we had a small regression last quarter with a quality drift.
[00:07:09] Maya: we can include a quality monitoring clause where we run evals on release rollouts; automatic rollback or notification can be part of the SLA. legal usually frames it as response times and mitigations rather than absolute liability.
[00:07:22] Priya: yes the eval hooks + rollback policy would be great.
[00:07:25] Maya: ok i'm going to recap next steps now.
[00:07:28] Maya: recap: maya sends pricing matrix + amendment draft; ethan runs benchmarks and evals on the prompt set; customer to upload anonymized prompts and confirm region list and RPS; security artifacts (SOC2, network diagrams) uploaded by maya; target sign-off by 8/25 to kick provisioning.
[00:07:44] Jordan: that aligns with us. one more ask — can you include an option to trial a small eu dedicated node for 2 weeks at reduced rate to validate latency?
[00:07:52] Maya: yes we can include a pilot option in the amendment.
[00:07:55] Priya: perfect.
[00:07:58] Maya: awesome, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the benchmark kickoff and send the docs. thanks everyone.
[00:08:04] Jordan: thanks.
[00:08:06] Samir: thanks all.
[00:08:08] Ethan: thanks.

End of transcript.
